text:
Jia: heads-up — ap-southeast1 gpu-provisioner holding ~120 jobs. Reason shows local-nvme-io + cleaner retries after brief network partitions. IOPS spike -> attach failures. Anyone oncall?
Michael: seeing the same. metrics: node iops > 550k for multiple nodes. scratch-cleaner entered 3x loops, lots of tiny writes. Logs attached.
Alex: pinging @ops-bot — any recent scrub-controller deploys to that region?
ops-bot: deploy event: scrub-controller v1.12.4 rolled to ap-southeast1 at 1823334400 by ci/cd. No auto-rollback.
Priya: @net-bot any packetloss or flaps in ap-southeast1 around 1823334300-1823334400?
net-bot: brief BGP flap observed 1823334305–1823334350, ~0.4% packetloss on spine for AZ-1. Reconnects/ARPs noted.
Jia: timestamps line up. hypothesis: cleaner RPCs retried on RPC timeouts -> duplicate janitor runs -> hot stripes -> write amplification -> nvme iops surge -> attach hold.
Alex: mitigation suggestion: throttle scrub rate for affected pools and reduce concurrency. Command: `scrubctl set-rate --pool scratchpool-ap1 --rate 50` to dampen. Anyone able to run?
Michael: running it now on the 6 impacted hosts. Also shifting ~30 queued GPU attach requests to warm dedicated nodes to unblock latency-sensitive jobs.
Priya: if we move to dedicated warm nodes we'll incur incremental cost — what's the ballpark? Need to flag to finance if sustained.
Jia: short-term estimate: +2 dedicated gpus for ~2 hours ≈ $320. Cheaper than potential SLO breaches.
Alex: after throttle: measured iops dropped from ~560k -> ~180k within 90s on the worst host. Cleaner loops reduced. Leaving rate=50 for now and monitoring.
Michael: documenting hypothesis and next steps in a mini PM. Root cause candidate: scrub-controller doesn't exponential-backoff on RPC timeout during net flaps, causing redundant work. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/scrub-controller/pull/4523 (adds backoff + idempotency guard).
Priya: thanks. I'll coordinate with networking to add BGP dampening and schedule a canary rollout of PR-4523 to ap-southeast1 tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Michael, can you own the canary deploy?
Michael: yup, I'll do the canary and watch attach latencies.
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-0322-031 — assigned to Michael, Priya, Alex. Severity: LOW->MED until canary completes.
net-bot: BGP dampening maintenance window scheduled 2026-03-23 02:00 UTC. Impact should reduce micro-flap retries.
Jia: will keep monitoring provisioning queue and nvme iops. Thanks all :eyes:
